title: Grief Is Not a Lack of Faith

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Sarah lived to be a hundred and twenty-seven years old. She died at Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep over her. - Gen 23:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Sarah, the wife of the father of faith, the mother of the promised son, dies at the age of a hundred and twenty-seven. And notice what Abraham does: "Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep over her." The great man of faith weeps. He grieves openly, deeply, without shame. Scripture does not hide his tears.

This is important for us to see. Sometimes believers imagine that strong faith means we shouldn't grieve - that tears somehow show a lack of trust in God. But here is Abraham, whose faith we have watched grow through decades, weeping over the loss of his wife. Faith and grief are not opposites. Deep love produces deep sorrow when that love is parted by death.

We are meant to mourn. God made us to love, and where there is love, loss brings genuine pain. To weep over someone we have lost is not faithlessness; it is love honouring what it has lost. Even Jesus, standing at the tomb of His friend Lazarus, "wept" (John 11:35) - and He knew He was about to raise him.

So if you are grieving, do not add guilt to your sorrow by thinking you shouldn't feel it. Bring your tears honestly before God. Christians grieve, but "not... like the rest of mankind, who have no hope" (1 Thess 4:13). We weep - and we weep as people who trust in the God of resurrection. Grief and hope can dwell in the same heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you felt guilty for grieving, as though it showed weak faith?
- Can you bring your tears honestly to God, grieving with hope?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that grief is not a lack of faith. When I mourn, help me bring my tears honestly to You, without shame. Let me grieve as one who still trusts in You, the God of hope and resurrection.
Amen.
